title: The Stone That Opened a Door
paragraphs: In seventeen ninety nine, French soldiers in Egypt found a large stone near the town of Rosetta. The stone had the same message written three times. One version used Greek letters, and two others used ancient Egyptian writing.

Few people could read the Egyptian signs at that time, but many could read Greek. So the Greek lines gave scholars a key to the other two. Britain took the stone after the French army lost, and it has been in the British Museum since eighteen oh two.

In eighteen twenty two, a French scholar named Champollion showed how to read the Egyptian signs. After that, people could finally read the old writing on temples and tombs. Their work started a new chapter in the study of ancient Egypt. Because of this stone, a lost language could speak again.

sources.claim: Taş 1799'da Mısır'da Fransız askerlerce bulundu; aynı metin hiyeroglif, Demotik ve Yunanca olmak üzere üç yazıyla yazılıydı.
